body: Two layers. (1) Sector/stock contrarianism: buy what has underperformed for years and is unloved (ICICI Pru describes buying underperformers in mid/small caps when they are cheap), avoid what everyone owns. (2) Valuation-based asset allocation: reduce equity (especially mid/small caps) when broad valuations and froth indicators are high; add when they are low; use debt and gold as ballast. His 2025-26 public warnings cited mid/small-cap median P/E ~43x (Feb 2025) and the 1994-2004 'lost decade' as the risk analogue. Individual version: a written rule, e.g., target equity 50-80% stepping down as Nifty trailing P/E rises above ~24 and smallcap P/E premium widens, stepping up below ~18; rebalance annually. Evidence: Indian studies show 5-year returns are weak from Nifty P/E above ~24 (see insight:india-valuation-forward-returns); timing signals are early, so steps beat all-or-nothing switches.
title: Naren: buy underperformers, allocate by valuation
